subject.title: feat: provider fallback by failure class — quarantine auth-broken providers

question: What default provider/profile incident policy should OpenClaw use for hard auth failures versus transient 401s, and what redacted status surface should expose that state?
rationale: Current main has classifiers and partial mitigation, but changing auth quarantine defaults, transient-401 handling, and status visibility changes provider routing, session behavior, and operator diagnostics.

options.title: Default incident-health model
options.body: Implement hard-auth quarantine only after a documented confirmation boundary, preserve transient 401 recovery, and add redacted status or doctor visibility.

options.title: Keep opt-in skip only
options.body: Leave default fallback behavior unchanged and improve models/status guidance, accepting repeated auth attempts unless operators configure skip TTL.

options.title: Split restart subcase first
options.body: Repair the auth-rewarm config-write restart loop separately before deciding the broader provider quarantine policy.

recommendation.title: Default incident-health model
recommendation.body: Implement hard-auth quarantine only after a documented confirmation boundary, preserve transient 401 recovery, and add redacted status or doctor visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this decision to fallback observability, OAuth auth read-through, status helpers, and model/auth reporting across the affected surfaces.
